text:
acme-app: Hey team — since yesterday our service in prod VPC can't reliably reach the Redwood API through the Interface VPC Endpoint. We see TLS cert name mismatch in the client logs and about 30% of requests timeout. Started after we routed some subnets through a NAT GW for outbound logging. Any idea?

sara.support: Hi! Can you paste the exact client error and a couple quick network checks (dig/curl/traceroute) from a failing instance? Also which endpoint (vpce-...) and whether Private DNS was enabled?

acme-app: Error from our Go client: "x509: certificate is valid for api.redwood-inference.com, not vpce-1234-abcdef.amazonaws.com".
We ran: 
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal
54.213.55.11
$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal 2>&1 | sed -n '1,120p'
* Connected to 54.213.55.11 (54.213.55.11) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
* server certificate name "api.redwood-inference.com" does not match requested host name "api.redwood-inference.internal".
```
Also traceroute shows path leaving via the NAT: 
```
traceroute to 54.213.55.11 (54.213.55.11), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.2.1 (10.0.2.1)  0.2 ms
 2  10.0.1.1 (10.0.1.1)  1.0 ms
 3  * * *
 4  54.213.55.11  12 ms
```

acme-app: Our endpoint is vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7; Private DNS was NOT enabled initially (we recently toggled some DNS settings).

sara.support: Ok — two likely issues here: 1) DNS is resolving to a public IP (54.213...), so traffic goes out via the NAT and back in => TLS SNI mismatch and likely IP allowlist problems. 2) Hairpin routing through NAT means source IPs become the NAT public IP which may be rejected by endpoint SGs or upstream allowlists.

jay.sre: Quick checks: are you using the endpoint's interface ENI IPs in the same subnet? Also check if the VPC endpoint has Private DNS enabled (that resolves the service name to the endpoint ENIs). If Private DNS is off, the DNS name will resolve to the public service IP.

acme-app: We had Private DNS off for testing. We flipped it on just now but still see intermittent failures (some instances are fine, some not).

alex.infra: If you flipped Private DNS, ensure DNS cache was cleared on the instances or restart the service. Also check /etc/resolv.conf and that the DHCP option set points to the VPC resolver. For the ones still failing, run:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @169.254.169.253
10.0.45.12
```
If you get a private ENI IP (10.0.x.x) that's good. If it still returns 54.213.x.x then split-horizon/resolution isn't applied (or you have host overrides).

acme-app: For failing host we still got 54.213.55.11. We also use an outbound proxy on some hosts that forces traffic through the NAT even for private addresses. Could that cause hairpin?

sara.support: Yes — outbound proxies or explicit egress routing to NAT will cause hairpin. The endpoint expects connections to stay inside the VPC and go to the ENI IP. If traffic is forced out, you'll hit the public front door which serves a cert for the public name (hence the mismatch).

jay.sre: Additional verification: run a tcpdump to confirm the destination IP and source IP:
```
sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 host 54.213.55.11 or host 10.0.45.12 -c 50
```
Look for src IP being 10.0.x.x (good) vs your NAT public IP (bad).

acme-app: We found two classes of hosts: app-subnet ones that go via the proxy/NAT and infra-subnet ones that go direct. App-subnet reads 54.213... and infra reads 10.0.45.12.

alex.infra: Fix options (ordered by recommended):
1) Ensure Private DNS is enabled on the VPC Endpoint and restart DNS cache / services so the name resolves to the endpoint ENIs.
2) Remove/whitelist the endpoint's private ENI CIDRs from any outbound proxy/egress rules so traffic to the service doesn't go via the NAT. If you use an explicit proxy, add a NO_PROXY for the endpoint domain.
3) If you must go via NAT (e.g., cross-account routing), use a VPC endpoint policy + security group rules that allow the NAT's public IP or use a dedicated NAT per service and update allowlists on Redwood side (ask enterprise team).

sara.support: One more gotcha — if you are peered/transit-gw routing from other VPCs, enable the endpoint in the VPC where the callers are, or use endpoint service acceptance in the provider. Interface endpoints are regional and per-VPC; DNS won’t automatically resolve to ENIs across peering unless you configure Route 53 resolver rules.

acme-app: We had some callers from a peered logging VPC — that explains the intermittent pattern.

jay.sre: For immediate mitigation: on failing hosts, add a host entry mapping the API host to the endpoint ENI IP (temporary):
```
10.0.45.12 api.redwood-inference.internal
```
And clear DNS cache. Not ideal but good for quick rollback. Longer term fix the proxy/egress rules and use the VPC endpoint properly.

acme-app: Thanks, we'll try disabling the proxy for the endpoint CDN and enable Private DNS across the VPCs + clear caches. We'll report back.

sara.support: Great — ping here with the dig/curl output after changes and we can check logs on our side (if you include timestamp and request IDs). :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-09T14:23:01Z completed to prod (no infra changes to VPC endpoints).

acme-app: Follow-up — after enabling Private DNS and adding NO_PROXY the errors dropped to <1% and SNI mismatch is gone. Still seeing a handful of 403 from one NATed IP — opening a ticket to get that IP allowlisted on your side.

sara.support: Logged. Can you DM the public IP to us and we will coordinate allowlist/ing with infra. Also we'll double-check the endpoint policy/SGs on vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7.

acme-app: Sent the IP. Thanks for the help!
